tools.name: search_tenders
tools.description: Search open public procurement tenders (government tenders, госзакупки, тендеры) from official portals: EU TED and Armenia ARMEPS (armeps.am, gnumner.am). Free text in English, Russian or Armenian, optional filters: country, CPV/OKPD2 codes, budget, deadline. Returns up to 20 short cards; "subject"

tools.name: get_tender
tools.description: Get the full card of one tender: status, deadline, budget, what is procured (subject), lots with prices and CPV codes, links to tender documents. Use the id from search_tenders results. On the Free plan, CPV codes, lots and document links are omitted.

tools.name: add_to_watchlist
tools.description: Save a query and filters as a watchlist for ongoing monitoring; new, amended and closing-soon matching tenders are then sent by email (Free plan: daily digest) and/or a signed HTTPS webhook (Pro plan). Returns watchlistId and how many open tenders match right now. Each call creates a new watchlist (

tools.name: get_deadline_alerts
tools.description: List alerts from your watchlists for the last 30 days on tenders that are still open, nearest deadline first (up to 50). Does not mark alerts as read. Empty until you create a watchlist with add_to_watchlist.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: add_to_watchlist · Private data: search_tenders, get_tender · Public sink: add_to_watchlist · Destructive: add_to_watchlist.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: add_to_watchlist · Private data: search_tenders, get_tender · Public sink: add_to_watchlist · Destructive: add_to_watchlist

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
